title: WSO2 Releases Agent Manager as Enterprises Look to Control Growing AI Agent Sprawl
gist: WSO2 shipped the general-availability release of Agent Manager, a framework-independent governance layer for AI agents covering identity, MCP policy, and a Kubernetes-native sandbox, reflecting an industry-wide shift where agent governance is being treated as a platform problem no single vendor yet fully solves.

insights.claim: As organizations build AI agents across an expanding range of models and frameworks, the infrastructure used to manage those agents' identity, permissions, behavior, and lifecycle is often fragmented, creating a governance gap distinct from the challenge of building the agents themselves.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Fragmented agent governance is a structural cost center enterprises will need to budget for separately from AI model spend as agent deployments scale.
insights.locator: The release addresses a growing enterprise challenge

insights.claim: Because AI agents can invoke tools, access APIs, delegate work, and interact with other agents, they raise new questions of authority and accountability that conventional applications never had to answer.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Agent-to-agent delegation breaks identity models built for human-to-system or system-to-system access, forcing a new non-human-identity layer.
insights.locator: Unlike conventional applications, agents can invoke tools

insights.claim: WSO2 released the general availability of Agent Manager, an open-source platform providing centralized governance, identity management, security controls, and operational oversight for AI agents running across different models, frameworks, and deployment environments.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: An open-source governance layer lowers the cost of adopting agent controls, which could accelerate enterprise agent deployment by removing a compliance blocker.
insights.locator: WSO2 has announced the general availability of WSO2 Agent Manager

insights.claim: WSO2's core design principle separates agent governance from agent logic, so common controls can be applied independently of the underlying AI model, framework, or runtime being used.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral governance lets enterprises swap or mix models and frameworks without rebuilding identity and policy controls each time, reducing lock-in risk.
insights.locator: WSO2's approach separates agent governance from agent logic

insights.claim: Agent Manager entered beta in June 2026, and its general availability release adds deeper agent identity capabilities, governance controls for Model Context Protocol interactions, and a Kubernetes-native sandboxed runtime.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A roughly three-month beta-to-GA cycle signals WSO2 is moving fast to capture the current enterprise agent-governance land grab.
insights.locator: Agent Manager entered beta in June 2026

insights.claim: Agent Manager provides more than 40 built-in controls, including personally identifiable information masking and rate limiting, which can be applied across the agent, MCP, and LLM layers of a workflow.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Enforcing PII masking and rate limiting at multiple layers (agent, MCP, LLM) rather than just at the model boundary gives more granular compliance coverage.
insights.locator: The platform provides more than 40 built-in controls

insights.claim: Agent Manager includes lifecycle controls for moving agents through development, staging, and production, the ability to suspend agents when required, and evaluation capabilities using rule-based and LLM-based checks to detect unexpected token consumption, behavioral changes, or declining response quality.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Treating agent behavioral drift and token-consumption anomalies as monitorable metrics turns agent reliability into an operational discipline rather than an ad hoc concern.
insights.locator: Agent Manager also uses OpenTelemetry for tracing

insights.claim: WSO2 built Agent Manager to support multiple agent frameworks and providers including LangChain, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure, Ballerina, and custom-built agents, using open standards such as OpenTelemetry, MCP, and OAuth 2 extensions.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Broad framework support is a direct bet that enterprises will run heterogeneous agent stacks rather than standardize on one vendor's ecosystem.
insights.locator: WSO2's approach is built around framework and model independence

insights.claim: The wider industry conversation suggests agent governance is increasingly becoming a platform problem rather than simply an AI development problem, with AWS, Microsoft, and other providers all adding combinations of non-human identity, tool authorization, policy enforcement, runtime isolation, observability, and evaluation to their own agent platforms.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Major cloud vendors converging on the same governance feature set signals this is becoming a required layer of any enterprise agent stack, not an optional add-on.
insights.locator: The wider industry conversation suggests that agent governance

insights.claim: Industry analysis from Qovery argues no single platform yet provides a complete governance stack across every layer, meaning enterprises are likely to combine identity systems, policy engines, infrastructure control planes, and isolated runtimes from different vendors rather than consolidate on one.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: If no single vendor can offer a complete stack, the near-term winners may be interoperability and standards (MCP, OAuth 2 extensions) rather than any one governance platform.
insights.locator: Recent industry analysis from Qovery has also argued

insights.claim: A framework-independent control plane becomes increasingly relevant as organizations' agent estates are expected to span multiple models and cloud platforms rather than settle on a single provider.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: This favors governance-layer vendors positioned as neutral infrastructure over model or cloud vendors trying to bundle governance with their own agent stack.
insights.locator: That makes the idea of a framework-independent control plane

insights.claim: The emerging challenge in enterprise AI is now less about how to build agents and more about how to consistently identify, govern, and control them once they are operating at scale, echoing earlier shifts in cloud and platform engineering where technology diversity still required common controls around identity, security, policy, observability, and lifecycle management.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Frames agent governance spend as a recurring platform-engineering line item analogous to cloud governance tooling, useful for sizing the addressable market.
insights.locator: The emerging challenge is therefore similar to earlier shifts
